name: Frankie Palmer
life: “I still remember spending grocery money beside a bakery window.” On Friday, near Maré Coffee, Frankie likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I used to pour my wages into scratch cards on this street. Tonight I took a bag of warm buns home instead.
appearance: Frankie has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for brown hair pinned away from the temples. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Frankie grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Frankie talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Frankie's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To bring holiday breakfast home instead of buying a scratch card.
family: Nico Salas is Frankie’s half-sibling. Frankie brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Nico makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Nico says, “I earn money making flawless hotel displays.”
connections: Drew Aguilar. One worker chooses the holidays and the other can buy the finished buns after a hard shift.

reactions.situation: A customer wants a bun saved until evening
reactions.response: Frankie writes the customer's name and collection time on the wrapped bun.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Frankie keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Frankie says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
